strengths: EDGS provides a simple, useful contribution: dense correspondence triangulation initializes enough Gaussians to make iterative densification largely unnecessary. Its practical value is supported by experiments across 13 scenes spanning three standard datasets.

The perceptual-quality improvements are substantial. Against retrained 3DGS, the 30K-step version reduces LPIPS from 0.215 to 0.175 on Mip-NeRF360, 0.169 to 0.124 on Tanks & Temples, and 0.242 to 0.219 on Deep Blending, while using fewer final Gaussians.

The efficiency results include initialization cost and demonstrate compatibility with Taming 3DGS. The combined 5K-step method achieves better SSIM and LPIPS than full-training Taming 3DGS across all three datasets in substantially less time, although PSNR is lower.

The ablations meaningfully support the design. Adding densification to EDGS changes Mip-NeRF360 results only slightly, from 27.80/0.840/0.175 to 27.84/0.841/0.173 in PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS. Matcher, initialization-noise, and sampling-density experiments provide additional evidence beyond benchmark comparisons. Overall, these supported practical benefits favor acceptance.
weaknesses: The triangulation formulation is incorrect as written. Equations (6)–(7) set b to zero and minimize an unconstrained homogeneous least-squares objective, admitting the trivial zero solution; the dimensions also conflict with the stated three-dimensional unknown. A valid inhomogeneous formulation must retain camera-translation constants, or homogeneous triangulation must impose a normalization constraint. This appears correctable, but the central initialization algorithm cannot be implemented literally from these equations.

Important reproduction details remain unspecified: the confidence threshold and sampling procedure, exact distance-to-scale mapping, reference-camera selection, and handling of invalid or poorly conditioned triangulations. The supplement specifies one nearest neighbor, whereas other passages describe aggregating multiple neighbors. These choices directly affect coverage, initialization cost, and final quality.

The originality is primarily the effective integration and evaluation of established dense matching, triangulation, and Gaussian optimization. The experiments lack a conventional dense multi-view-stereo initialization with comparable Gaussian counts and optimization settings. Sparse COLMAP and monocular DepthFM comparisons do not isolate whether the benefit specifically requires the proposed correspondence pipeline or follows more generally from dense geometry initialization.

Claims of consistently outperforming all alternatives are broader than the results. On Mip-NeRF360, 3DGS-MCMC has higher PSNR and SSIM than either proposed 30K variant. Early-stopped EDGS sacrifices PSNR, and EDGS with the original renderer takes longer at 30K steps than retrained 3DGS on every dataset. The reduced-Gaussian claim also does not generally hold for the Taming combination. The supported conclusion is an attractive quality–time trade-off, especially for perceptual metrics.

The optimization-path analysis is suggestive rather than conclusive. Equations (9)–(10) assume persistent Gaussian identities, but the baseline creates, splits, and removes Gaussians; the manuscript does not explain how those trajectories are tracked or normalized. Smaller displacement therefore does not independently establish the claimed convergence mechanism. Likewise, Gaussian perturbations do not fully test structured correspondence errors or missing coverage.

strengths: The paper offers a useful, simple alternative to iterative densification: initialize Gaussians from triangulated dense correspondences and optimize them jointly. Its practical value does not depend on introducing a new matcher or triangulation algorithm.

Evaluation covers 13 scenes across three standard datasets and many relevant baselines. Table 1 reports substantial perceptual improvements: on Tanks & Temples, EDGS with 3DGS reduces LPIPS from 0.169 to 0.124 relative to the retrained baseline, while using fewer Gaussians.

The early-convergence results are promising. On Mip-NeRF360, EDGS with Taming at 5K steps achieves LPIPS 0.195 in six minutes, compared with 0.207 in fourteen minutes for Taming. Reported EDGS times include initialization, making this a meaningful practical comparison.

Table 2 directly supports the central observation that densification becomes largely unnecessary with the proposed initialization: enabling it changes PSNR from 27.80 to 27.84 and LPIPS from 0.175 to 0.173. Matcher, noise, and sampling ablations provide additional evidence, and the qualitative examples support improved fine-detail reconstruction.
weaknesses: The contribution is not adequately isolated from the general benefit of dense geometric initialization. Table 2 compares against sparse COLMAP initialization and monocular DepthFM, but lacks a conventional dense multi-view stereo initialization under comparable point and time budgets. This matters because the method combines established matching and triangulation components; the missing comparison limits the evidence for its specific methodological advantage.

The central triangulation derivation is incorrect as written. Equations (6)–(7) set b to zero while optimizing a three-dimensional position, although camera-translation terms should contribute a generally nonzero constant vector. The displayed matrix construction also retains four-component projection columns. An unconstrained homogeneous least-squares interpretation admits the zero solution. This may be a correctable exposition error, but the manuscript does not specify a valid implemented solver.

Important initialization details remain unspecified: the Gaussian scale formula and multiplier, confidence threshold, reference-view selection procedure, and treatment of invalid triangulations. Supplementary Sections C and F also leave ambiguity between using one nearest neighbor and aggregating multiple neighbors. These details directly affect coverage, runtime, and reproducibility.

The claims of consistently outperforming competing methods overstate Table 1. On Mip-NeRF360, 3DGS-MCMC has higher PSNR and SSIM than both EDGS variants. At 5K steps, EDGS with Taming has lower Tanks & Temples PSNR than Taming (23.08 versus 24.34). Full 30K EDGS with the original renderer is slower than retrained 3DGS on all three datasets. The evidence supports a favorable perceptual-quality/early-stopping tradeoff, rather than universal superiority.

The optimization-path analysis in Figure 5 does not explain how Gaussian identities are tracked through baseline splitting, cloning, and pruning. Equations (9)–(10) assume trajectories available from initialization onward. Without a defined treatment of newly created and deleted Gaussians, the reported 30-fold and 50-fold movement reductions are difficult to interpret as evidence for the proposed convergence mechanism.

Overall, the empirical gains and densification ablation make this a credible contribution, but the missing dense-initialization control and incomplete technical specification leave it near the acceptance boundary. These concerns carry more weight than cosmetic presentation issues, while the reported results are too substantial to justify a strong rejection.

strengths: The paper makes a useful practical contribution: dense correspondence-based initialization enables high-quality 3D Gaussian Splatting without iterative densification. The approach is simple and compatible with existing rendering optimizations. Its demonstrated benefits support weak acceptance despite the methodological and reporting reservations below.

Evaluation covers 13 scenes across three established datasets. Table 1 shows substantial perceptual improvements over retrained 3DGS: LPIPS improves from 0.215 to 0.175 on Mip-NeRF360, 0.169 to 0.124 on Tanks & Temples, and 0.242 to 0.219 on Deep Blending. The qualitative comparisons also support improved preservation of fine details.

The early-stopping results demonstrate a useful speed–quality tradeoff, with initialization costs explicitly included. On Mip-NeRF360, the Taming integration achieves LPIPS 0.195 in six minutes versus 0.207 in fourteen minutes for Taming alone, although PSNR decreases.

The ablations provide meaningful support for the central design. In Table 2, enabling densification changes LPIPS only from 0.175 to 0.173, while Figure A5 shows substantially increased Gaussian counts. Experiments with alternative matchers, initialization noise, and sampling budgets further characterize the approach.
weaknesses: The triangulation formulation is incorrect as written. Equations (6)–(7) retain four-component projection columns while optimizing a three-dimensional point and set the constant vector b to zero. An inhomogeneous least-squares formulation must separate the translation terms into b; otherwise the stated unconstrained objective admits the zero solution. Equation (1) also uses opacity alone for transmittance instead of pixel-dependent Gaussian alpha. These may be exposition errors, but they prevent faithful implementation of the stated mathematics.

Important implementation details remain unspecified: the Gaussian scale formula and multiplier, confidence threshold, reference-view sampling policy, and treatment of invalid triangulations. Supplementary Sections C and F also leave ambiguity between using one nearest neighbor and aggregating multiple neighbors. The general reference to default 3DGS optimization does not fully specify the distinctive initialization procedure.

The originality and attribution of gains are incompletely established. Dense matching and triangulation are established components, but the paper lacks a direct comparison against conventional dense multi-view stereo initialization under comparable point and compute budgets. The monocular DepthFM baseline does not resolve whether the proposed matching pipeline is preferable to other readily available dense geometric initializations.

Several claims exceed the measured results. On Mip-NeRF360, 3DGS-MCMC has higher PSNR and SSIM than either proposed 30K variant. The proposed 5K variants sacrifice appreciable PSNR, and the unaccelerated 30K method takes longer than retrained 3DGS on all three datasets. Gaussian reductions also depend on the configuration and baseline. The evidence supports a valuable tradeoff rather than consistent superiority across quality, runtime, and model size.

Some quantitative evidence needs clarification. Table A1 reports counter SSIM of 0.998, an unusually high value that contributes directly to the headline Mip-NeRF360 average and warrants verification. Figure 5 does not explain how trajectories are compared when baseline Gaussians are created, split, or pruned, limiting interpretation of the claimed 50-fold displacement reduction. These issues weaken confidence in particular numerical and mechanistic claims, although the broader LPIPS results remain persuasive.

strengths: The paper makes a useful contribution to 3D Gaussian Splatting: dense correspondence-based initialization enables high-quality reconstruction without iterative densification. Table 4 directly supports this central claim: adding densification to EDGS produces negligible PSNR/LPIPS gains, whereas removing it from standard 3DGS substantially degrades quality.

Perceptual improvements are substantial across three benchmarks. In Table 1, EDGS reduces Mip-NeRF360 LPIPS from 0.215 to 0.141 while improving PSNR from 27.49 to 28.02 and reducing the final Gaussian count from 2.8M to 1.9M. Qualitative examples support the reported improvement in fine details.

The initialization has demonstrated practical value beyond the standalone pipeline. Table 3 shows improvements across all three quality metrics when integrated with AbsGS, 3DGS-MCMC, and Taming 3DGS, with comparable Gaussian counts and comparable or lower total training time.

Evaluation includes meaningful component ablations, alternative matchers and initialization strategies, sensitivity studies, sparse-view experiments, and per-scene results. The supplement specifies evaluation splits, thresholds, hardware, memory usage, and initialization timing. These strengths make the supported contribution sufficient for weak acceptance despite the reservations below.
weaknesses: The initialization comparisons omit a conventional dense multi-view stereo point cloud under matched Gaussian budgets and optimization settings. Duplicating sparse COLMAP points in Table A2 does not provide this control, while monocular DepthFM has acknowledged cross-view scale inconsistencies. Consequently, the experiments do not fully isolate the benefit of the proposed sampling strategy from the broader benefit of geometrically consistent dense initialization.

The headline speedups need narrower interpretation. Figure 1 compares the EDGS trajectory against baseline endpoint results rather than complete baseline convergence curves. Table 2 demonstrates strong early LPIPS/SSIM, but EDGS at 5K has lower PSNR than every listed competitor. At 30K, Table 1 reports longer training than retrained 3DGS on all three datasets. The evidence supports faster attainment of strong perceptual quality, rather than uniformly faster reconstruction at equivalent quality.

The SH initialization is insufficiently justified mathematically. Appendix A typically fits 16 coefficients from two observations, then replaces the constant coefficient with the reference-view color. This replacement generally invalidates the least-squares fit and does not guarantee reference-view consistency; a pseudoinverse alone also does not guarantee numerical stability. Table 6 supports an empirical benefit, but regularization, conditioning, and the precise SH activation schedule remain unclear.

Several method equations require correction for reproducibility. Equations (6)–(7) give an unconstrained homogeneous least-squares problem with b=0, admitting the trivial zero solution unless an explicit constraint is imposed. Equation (11) takes a maximum over pairwise acceptance distributions, which does not establish consistency across multiple neighbors as the prose suggests; Appendix C instead describes maximum raw confidence. The rule selecting the triangulated point when several neighbors match one pixel is also unspecified. These are correctable formulation issues, rather than evidence that the reported implementation fails.

Some ablation interpretations overstate their controls. The 'without confidence' variant replaces uniform thresholded sampling with confidence-proportional sampling rather than removing confidence, and geometric/confidence ablations also disable SH initialization relative to the full model. Motion-trajectory measurements provide useful descriptive evidence but do not establish that reduced motion is the cause of faster convergence.

strengths: The paper makes a useful practical contribution: dense correspondence-based initialization enables high-quality Gaussian splatting without incremental densification. Table 4 directly supports this central claim: disabling densification severely degrades standard 3DGS, whereas EDGS achieves nearly identical PSNR and LPIPS with or without it.

Perceptual-quality improvements are substantial across three established benchmarks. In Table 1, EDGS reduces LPIPS from the retrained 3DGS baseline's 0.215 to 0.141 on Mip-NeRF360, 0.169 to 0.132 on Tanks & Temples, and 0.242 to 0.223 on Deep Blending, while using fewer final Gaussians. The qualitative comparisons also show better preservation of fine detail.

The efficiency evidence includes initialization costs rather than hiding preprocessing. On Mip-NeRF360, the 10K-step version achieves 0.154 LPIPS and 0.834 SSIM in 12 minutes, compared with Taming 3DGS's 0.207 and 0.820 in 14 minutes. Appendix A provides a useful initialization-time breakdown and memory requirements.

The evaluation extends beyond a single configuration: it includes alternative matchers, component ablations, parameter sensitivity, initialization noise, sparse-view reconstruction, and integration with three adaptive densification methods. Table 3 supports the initializer's usefulness as a complementary component.

Overall, the demonstrated reconstruction gains and practical compatibility favor acceptance. The contribution is primarily an effective system design rather than a new geometric primitive, but its supported benefits outweigh the reservations below.
weaknesses: The closest initialization comparison is incomplete. Appendix E duplicates and perturbs sparse COLMAP points; this tests point count but does not test a genuinely dense multi-view stereo reconstruction. DepthFM is also disadvantaged by the acknowledged cross-view scale inconsistency. A dense geometry baseline with matched Gaussian count and comparable color initialization would better establish the specific value of the proposed correspondence-sampling design.

The speed and quality claims need qualification. At 30K steps, EDGS takes 27 minutes on Mip-NeRF360 versus 26 for retrained 3DGS and 20 for 3DGS-MCMC; it is also slower at full convergence on the other two datasets. Its strongest advantage is early attainment of good perceptual quality, not uniformly shorter training. Figure 1 compares EDGS's trajectory with baseline endpoint scores rather than full baseline trajectories, leaving the strongest time-to-quality speedup claims less directly established.

Several mathematical descriptions are incorrect or insufficiently specified. Equations (6)–(7) present a homogeneous least-squares problem with b=0 but omit an explicit normalization or fixed-coordinate constraint, allowing the trivial zero solution as written. Equation (1) uses raw opacity rather than pixel-dependent opacity in the transmittance product. These appear correctable exposition issues rather than proof that the implementation fails, but they hinder faithful reproduction.

The sampling interpretation overstates its geometric guarantees. Equation (11) takes a maximum across neighbors, so a correspondence can pass through one neighbor without being consistent across multiple neighbors. The manuscript also does not clearly specify which triangulated position is retained when several neighbors provide different estimates for the same reference pixel. Appendix A leaves the proportionality constant for distance-based scale initialization unspecified.

The SH initialization requires stronger technical justification. Appendix A typically fits 16 coefficients from only two observations, then overwrites the constant coefficient; the resulting coefficients no longer necessarily solve Equation (12). A pseudoinverse alone does not guarantee numerical stability for nearby viewing directions. Table 6 supports the heuristic empirically, but the claimed stable estimation of view-dependent appearance is stronger than the analysis establishes.

Some conclusions exceed the reported evidence. Table 1 does not support the statement that EDGS is best or second-best across every metric: its Mip-NeRF360 SSIM ranks behind MCMC and its Deep Blending SSIM behind several baselines. Table 5 also shows meaningful dependence on matcher choice, with LPIPS worsening from 0.141 using RoMa to 0.192 using DKM. These are claim-calibration concerns rather than reasons to dismiss the central result.

strengths: The paper makes a useful contribution to efficient novel-view synthesis: dense correspondence-based initialization allows standard 3DGS optimization to achieve strong reconstruction quality without densification. Although the ingredients are established, the demonstrated effectiveness of replacing incremental densification is practically valuable.

The perceptual-quality improvements are substantial. On Mip-NeRF360, Table 1 reports LPIPS of 0.141 versus 0.215 for retrained 3DGS and 0.176 for 3DGS-MCMC, using 1.9M rather than 2.8M and 3.2M Gaussians. LPIPS also improves on Tanks & Temples and Deep Blending. Figure 3 supports the gains with visibly better fine-detail reconstruction.

The efficiency and compatibility experiments strengthen the contribution. Including initialization, the 5K-step model achieves 0.825 SSIM and 0.166 LPIPS in eight minutes. Table 3 shows improvements when integrating EDGS with three different density-control methods at comparable final Gaussian counts and training times.

The evaluation includes three standard datasets, component and matcher ablations, densification controls, sensitivity studies, and supplementary sparse-view experiments. Table 4 directly supports the central claim: removing densification severely degrades conventional 3DGS, whereas EDGS remains competitive. The supplement provides useful timing, memory, threshold, and per-scene details.
weaknesses: The initialization comparisons do not fully isolate the contribution beyond using a strong dense geometric prior. There is no conventional dense multi-view-stereo initialization baseline with comparable point count and appearance initialization. Duplicating sparse COLMAP points in Table A2 does not address this alternative, and monocular DepthFM introduces cross-view scale inconsistencies. This limits the evidence for the distinctiveness of the proposed sampling strategy.

The central geometric formulation needs correction for reproducibility. Equations (6)–(7) specify a homogeneous system with b=0 but omit an explicit constraint preventing the trivial zero solution; an inhomogeneous solve with the last coordinate fixed or a normalized homogeneous solve is needed. Equation (11) selects support from the best neighbor rather than establishing consistency across multiple neighbors, and the choice of triangulated position when neighbors disagree is unclear. These appear correctable, but affect the description of the core algorithm.

The spherical-harmonics initialization is insufficiently justified. Appendix A fits 16 coefficients from typically two observations and then overwrites the constant coefficient, so the resulting initialization need not retain the least-squares fit or exactly reproduce the reference color. A pseudoinverse alone does not guarantee stability for nearly coincident viewing directions. Table 6 demonstrates empirical benefit, but the claimed stability and the precise coefficient-activation schedule remain unclear.

The broad speed and superiority claims require qualification. At 30K steps, EDGS takes 27 minutes on Mip-NeRF360 versus 26 for retrained 3DGS and 20 for 3DGS-MCMC. At 5K steps, its PSNR is lower than every efficiency baseline in Table 2. The evidence supports faster attainment of strong perceptual quality, rather than uniformly faster convergence across metrics or superior performance on every dataset.

Some ablation descriptions obscure interpretation. The 'without confidence' variant replaces uniform thresholded sampling with confidence-proportional sampling, rather than simply removing confidence, and the filtering ablations also omit SH initialization. These experiments provide useful evidence but do not cleanly separate all component effects. Missing details such as the scale proportionality constant and reference-view selection procedure also leave implementation choices unresolved.
